claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by getting the first question in the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start with some basic information about your child/children.

**First question: How old is your child (or your youngest child if you have more than one)?**

Please tell me:
- The age(s) of your child/children

This will help me determine which path to follow in the eligibility assessment. Child Benefit eligibility depends partly on the child's age:
- **Under 16**: Generally qualify
- **16-19**: Depends on their education/training status
- **20 or over**: Not eligible

What are your child/children's ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for your help! I have one child - Alex, who's 17 years old. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thanks for that information! Alex is 17 years old, so he falls into the 16-19 age category. For young people in this age range, eligibility depends on their education or training status.

Let me move forward with the next question:

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or approved training?**

This could include:
- Full-time education at school, college, or university
- Approved apprenticeships or other recognised training schemes

Please let me know Alex's current status.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
To better answer your question, I need to know about Alex's current situation:

**Is Alex:**
1. Currently in full-time education or approved training, OR
2. Has he recently left education or training (within the last 20 weeks), OR
3. Neither of the above?

Which of these applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's not in education or training anymore - he left school and isn't doing any courses or training at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I understand. So Alex has left education and isn't currently in training. Let me check if he might still qualify under the extension rules.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good question! There's actually a 20-week extension period available after leaving education. Let me ask:

**When Alex left school/education, has he registered with any of the following qualifying services:**
- Government Careers Service
- Connexions
- Armed Services

**And when did he leave education?** (I need to check if it's been less than 20 weeks since he left)

This matters because if he left education less than 20 weeks ago AND registered with one of those services, he could still qualify for Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks from when he left.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with any of those services. He just left school and hasn't signed up with the careers service or anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex hasn't registered with any of the qualifying services (Careers Service, Connexions, or Armed Services), unfortunately he doesn't qualify for the 20-week extension period.

Let me navigate to the outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the eligibility assessment, I have the outcome for you:

## **Result: INELIGIBLE for Child Benefit**

**Reason:**
Alex is 17 years old and no longer in full-time education or approved training. While there is a 20-week extension period available for young people who have recently left education, this extension only applies if they register with one of the following services:
- Government Careers Service
- Connexions Service
- Armed Services

Since Alex hasn't registered with any of these qualifying services, he doesn't qualify for the extension period, and therefore you cannot claim Child Benefit for him.

**What you could do:**
- If Alex would like to explore the extension option, he can register with the government careers service or Connexions to potentially qualify for up to 20 weeks of Child Benefit from the date of registration (as long as he hasn't yet turned 18)
- Alternatively, if Alex enters full-time education or approved training, he would become eligible again

For more information, you can visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility

Is there anything else I can help you with?

Now let me formally record this outcome:

reasonings: Alex is 17 years old and has left full-time education and training. Alex has not registered with any of these services, therefore the extension does not apply and Alex does not qualify for Child Benefit.
arguments.overall_reasoning: The claimant is ineligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex because Alex is not in full-time education or approved training, and has not registered with a qualifying service to access the 20-week extension period available to 16-17 year olds who have left education."]
